primary_claim: A novel fingerprinting algorithm that LoRA-embeds hidden log-probability signatures tied to a teacher model's top-k neuron activations can be detected in a logit-distilled student model (Qwen2.5-1.5B distilled from fingerprinted Qwen2.5-7B) at p<0.01 significance against a 1000-random-key null, and shows suggestive but sub-threshold signal (p=0.01-0.035) for hard-label distillation

effect.metric: standardized fingerprint detection score Z / one-sided Gaussian p-value vs. 1000-random-key null distribution
effect.value: logit-distilled student crosses detection threshold p<0.01; hard-label distilled: raw Z=2.273 (p=0.01152), reference-subtracted Z=1.811 (p=0.03507)

stated_future_work: more experiments with different model families and sizes to find whether fingerprinting improves, degrades, or stays static when scaling parameters and/or training samples
future, better provenance systems that allow frontier labs to provide valuable evidence when suspected violations occur
limitations_stated: hard-label distillation results do not reach the p<0.01 threshold used for the logit-based case, only nominal statistical significance
only tested on a single teacher/student pair (Qwen2.5-7B to Qwen2.5-1.5B) and a single dataset (PG-19)
quote: Only the student distilled from the fingerprinted teacher crosses the threshold among the operational suspect models.
